section: Introduction, inverse image, and RV definition
source_claims: Elementary outcomes can be complex; retain a numerical characteristic.
X maps Omega to R; X^{-1}(I) selects outcomes whose image is in I.
X is an RV when {X<b} is in A for every real b; interval preimages are then measurable.

evidence.transcript: 162.60-206.44 states X: Omega -> R; 228.78-339.90 defines inverse image and shorthand; 393.48-535.22 defines measurability; 590.32-679.36 gives the interval consequence.
evidence.board_or_ocr: board_004 (t=330): OCR records V=(Omega,A,P), X:Omega->R, X^{-1}(I) and {a<X<b}.

notes: Transcript ASR at 421.18 calls b a natural number, but the spoken/board context is b in R; body follows the displayed mathematical definition. No fidelity defect.

source_claims: For X,Y on the same probability space, cX, X+Y, X-Y, XY, and X/Y under P(Y=0)=0 are RVs.
For c<0, {cX<b}={X>b/c}.
{X+Y<b}=union over rational q of ({X<q} intersection {Y<b-q}); the nontrivial reverse inclusion is assigned to students.

evidence.transcript: 778.26-925.18 lists the closure claims and P(Y=0)=0; 970.42-1105.64 proves the negative-scalar case; 1123.00-1285.42 gives the rational-union identity and sigma-algebra argument; 1209.54-1235.26 assigns the remaining inclusion.
evidence.board_or_ocr: No formula dispute requiring further board inspection; transcript formulas are coherent.

notes: Body line 38 correctly states P(Y=0)=0 but immediately glosses it as no zero return. The source expressly distinguishes probability-zero occurrence from impossibility at 905.08-912.50. This is recorded for Stage B.

source_claims: 1_A maps A to 1 and A^c to 0.
Indicators turn intersection, union, and complement into product, inclusion-exclusion, and 1-1_A.
If A is measurable, 1_A is an RV by a three-case threshold calculation; indicators are measure/integration building blocks.

source_claims: Use distinct finite/countable values x_j and a measurable disjoint exhaustive family H_j.
X=sum_j x_j 1_{H_j} is discrete; one summand is nonzero for each omega.
The distribution is the values/probabilities table with p_j>0 and sum p_j=1; H_j may be written {X=x_j}.

evidence.transcript: 2332.86-2464.80 establishes values and full groups; 2513.14-2739.26 gives the definition and RV argument; 3615.96-3699.96 says H_j={X=x_j} and values are distinct; 3821.96-3964.98 defines distribution, p_j>0, and total one.

source_claims: Equal distribution means identical values/probabilities tables and can compare RVs from different spaces.
Processor capped at day 4000 aggregates tail mass at 4000 and is not equal in distribution to the unbounded model.
Fair coin coded 0/1 and parity of a fair die have the same distribution.

source_claims: X,Y must share one probability space to evaluate them at the same omega.
For g:R^2->R, Z=g(X,Y)=sum_{j,k}g(x_j,y_k)1_{H_j}1_{H_k^*}=sum_{j,k}g(x_j,y_k)1_{H_j intersection H_k^*}.

source_claims: Two discrete RVs on one V are independent iff every atom pair factors.
A family is mutually independent iff every selected subfamily (size at least two) and every configuration factors into the individual probabilities.
